subject: Commercial: Token commits, overages & discount structure — ACME RFP (Section 3)
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-03-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: ACME RFP — Section 3 (Commercial): Clarification on commits and overages

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick guide call yesterday. As we prepare final scoring for Section 3 (Commercial terms) of ACME's RFP, procurement has a few focused clarifications we need back by EOD Wednesday:

1) Token pricing: Please provide per-token unit price for text generation and embeddings, and whether these are measured per input token, output token, or combined.
2) Commit tiers: We need at least three annual commit scenarios (Conservative / Expected / Aggressive) with committed tokens, monthly billing profile, and any minimums.
3) Overage policy: If usage exceeds the monthly commit, what is the overage rate? Is there burst capacity with capped unit pricing?
4) Discounts & true-ups: Please outline discount schedule for higher commits, any volume thresholds, and whether unused committed tokens roll over or true-up at year-end.
5) Credit/termination: If ACME downgrades after year-one, do you offer transition credits or pro-rated refunds?

Attached: ACME_RFP_Section_3_Commercial.pdf — highlights the exact fields scoring looks for.

Can you also attach the commercial appendix in a single page summary? That helps the Sourcing Committee.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Senior Procurement Manager
ACME Corp

--
Attachment: ACME_RFP_Section_3_Commercial.pdf (PDF, 180KB)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-23T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME RFP — Section 3 (Commercial): Clarification on commits and overages

Elena —

Appreciate the clarity and timeline. See our commercial appendix attached and a concise summary below (high level figures so you can score against your matrix). I kept it to the specific items in your note. If you want a formal Excel with monthly ramp profiles, I can attach that by tomorrow.

Key assumptions (callouts): pricing below assumes inference on mid-sized generation models (equivalent to 70B FP16) with standard prompt+completion measurement (input + output tokens billed). Embeddings are billed separately. All prices exclude applicable taxes.

1) Token pricing (unit)
- Generation (prompt + completion): $0.0018 per token
- Embeddings: $0.0008 per embedding token

2) Commit scenarios (annual, pre-paid/committed spend)
- Conservative (C1): 120M tokens/year (~10M/mo) — effective unit price: $0.0016/token
- Expected (C2): 600M tokens/year (~50M/mo) — effective unit price: $0.0013/token
- Aggressive (C3): 2.4B tokens/year (~200M/mo) — effective unit price: $0.00095/token

Each scenario includes a monthly billing cadence with an agreed monthly committed token floor. Commits can be structured as annual pre-pay or monthly committed billing (with annual true-up).

3) Overage policy
- Monthly overages billed at 110% of the effective unit price for that tier (e.g., C2 overage = $0.00143/token).
- Burst capacity: we offer on-demand burst at the same overage rate up to 50% above monthly commit; beyond that we require a short-term (30-day) addendum for sustained increases.

4) Discounts & true-ups
- Volume discounts are built into the effective unit prices above. Additional strategic partner discounts: 5% off effective rate for multi-year commitments (2+ years) or if ACME purchases Redwood Optimize add-on.
- Unused committed tokens: up to 10% of committed tokens may roll month-to-month; annual true-up reconciles unused tokens and provides rollover credit (not a cash refund).

5) Credit / termination
- Early termination is subject to remaining committed spend for the year (standard industry practice). For enterprise reasons we offer a one-time transition credit equal to 10% of remaining committed spend if ACME migrates to a different vendor and provides 90 days notice.

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Tiers.pdf (one-page summary) and a draft Redwood_RFP_Response_Section3.docx with fields filled.

Next steps: if these figures match your scoring model, I can prepare a signed SOW template and a monthly ramp table. If Procurement wants a better blended price for the first year, Marissa is leading a concession request with Finance — tagging her here.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: ACME RFP — internal: concession request & approval path

On Mon, Mar 23, 2026 at 11:04 AM, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Tiers.pdf (PDF, 45KB); Redwood_RFP_Response_Section3.docx (DOCX, 27KB)

Quick internal —

We should consider a limited, time-bound welcome concession to secure ACME given the strategic fit. My proposal: 20% off the C2 effective unit price in year 1 (C2 is the $0.0013 token). That nets an effective blended price of $0.00104 for the first 12 months, then reverts to standard C2 pricing with the previously-stated true-up behavior. Conditions:
- Commit to C2 (600M tokens/year), 12-month initial term, auto-renew unless notice given 60 days prior.
- Concession contingent on Finance sign-off and an added clause limiting rollovers to 5% in year 1.

Finance margin check: Rishi — can you confirm whether this concession is acceptable without additional discounts on embedding pricing or SLAs? Also any constraint from Legal on transition credit language? We want to avoid unacceptable liability.

Marissa
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-03-25T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Final commercial summary — ACME RFP Section 3 (commits & overages)

Elena —

Thanks for the review window. Per our internal approvals, Redwood can offer the following commercial terms for ACME to include in your scored RFP submission:

Agreed commercial package (final)
- Baseline unit prices: Generation $0.0018/token; Embeddings $0.0008/token (billing measures input+output tokens for generation).
- Committed plan (selected): Expected (C2) — 600M tokens/year (50M/month). Effective unit price: $0.0013/token.
- Introductory concession: 20% discount applied to the C2 effective rate for year 1 only, final year-1 effective price = $0.00104/token. Conditions: 12-month initial term, enroll in annual true-up, 5% monthly rollover cap for year 1.
- Overage: Monthly overage billed at 110% of the applicable effective rate (year-1 concessioned rate where relevant). Burst capped at 50% above monthly commit at same overage rate.
- Multi-year: Additional 5% strategic discount available on execution of a 2-year committed agreement or purchase of Redwood Optimize.
- Early termination / transition: One-time transition credit 10% of remaining committed spend with 90 days notice; standard remaining-commit paydown applies otherwise.

Billing & operational notes
- Billing cadence: Monthly invoices, with an annual true-up reconciliation. Prepay options available for improved effective pricing and invoicing simplification.
- SLA credits and dispute path documented in the SOW.

Attachments & next steps
- Attached: Redwood_Pricing_Tiers.pdf (one-page), Redwood_RFP_Response_Section3.docx (completed section).
- I've created a HubSpot opportunity and a DocuSign SOW template; links below. If ACME approves these terms for scoring, we'll prepare the SOW and legal redlines for signature next week.

HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/record/ACME-12345
DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/templates/REDWOOD-ACME-2026

Would love a quick confirmation (email) that these terms are acceptable for scoring. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk the committee through mechanics.
